title: Performance Compass: per-route & per-model drilldown UI and chart specs
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Summary:
Design the 'Performance Compass' — a compact-to-expanded UI pattern for Redwood Console that surfaces per-route and per-model performance (latency percentiles, throughput, token metrics, and cost attribution), supports quick incident triage and informed rollouts, and provides exportable chart specs for engineering implementation.

Goals:
- Give engineers and SREs a single glanceable card that summarizes health and a consistent drill path into detailed timeseries and attribution.
- Support both high-density overview (compact cards on route lists) and a deeper modal/detail view (small multiples, comparisons across model variants and routes).
- Integrate rollout state (canary/baseline) visually and allow creating a rollout from the chart.
- Provide precise chart specs (metrics, sampling, expected tooltips, export CSV schema) so runtime/observability teams can implement without guesswork.

Primary user flows:
1) Glance: Support engineer scans the Console route list, sees per-route Performance Compass microcard with 3-line sparkline (P50 latency, throughput, avg tokens) and a colored health badge (green/amber/red).
2) Drill: Click a microcard → expanded panel with: stacked timeseries (throughput), overlay lines for P50/P95 latency, bar histogram for tokens distribution, and a cost ribbon.
3) Compare: Toggle 'Compare' to switch to small-multiples showing model variants side-by-side (same time range) for fast A/B or canary comparisons.
4) Rollout action: From the expanded chart, 'Create Rollout' button opens rollout composer prefilled with selected model+route and SLO thresholds.

Chart specs (engineer-friendly):
- Time resolution: 1-minute rollup for retention up to 24h; 5-minute rollup for 24h–30d.
- Primary charts in detail view (stacking order from back to front): throughput area (stacked by route or model variant), latency P95 line (thicker, hex color), latency P50 line (thinner, dashed), tokens per-request bar overlay (semi-transparent), cost ribbon (thin band along bottom).
- Latency: show P50 and P95 lines; moving average smoothing = 3-point EMA for display.
- Throughput: area chart with 95% bin shading; y-axis autoscale with optional fixed-mode toggle.
- Tokens: histogram aggregated per-minute with percentile markers (avg, p95).
- Sampling: display raw sample count in tooltip; if samples < 5 in a bucket, show '--' and a dotted outline to indicate low confidence.
- Tooltip content (order): timestamp, route, model, requests/sec, p50_ms, p95_ms, avg_tokens, p95_tokens, cost_usd_per_1k_tokens, sample_count.
- CSV export columns: timestamp, route, model, requests_rps, latency_p50_ms, latency_p95_ms, tokens_avg, tokens_p95, cost_usd.
- Visual thresholds: default latency SLO lines at 150ms (P50) and 300ms (P95) (configurable per-customer). Threshold rendering: faint dashed horizontal line with label and toggle to hide.
- Canary/rollout overlay: shaded vertical band(s) across the chart showing rollout windows; color-coded by variant (e.g., blue baseline, teal canary). Hover shows rollout name, percentage, start/end.
- Small multiples: tile layout (up to 6 across), shared x-axis zoom sync, independent y-axis by default with option to normalize.
- Accessibility: color palette must meet AA contrast for primary/secondary lines; ensure patterns (dashed/dotted) supplement color to differentiate lines for colorblind users.

Interaction details:
- Hover → sticky tooltip; click → lock tooltip and reveal 'open trace' / 'open logs' quick links.
- Drag+zoom horizontally to select range; selection updates the top-level period and updates other cards on the page (linked time context).
- Pin model or route to top of small-multiples for persistent comparison.
- Compact card collapse behavior: mobile collapses to single sparkline + health dot + baseline latency.

Styling guidelines (tokens):
- Primary latency (P95): #0B63E6 (blue), stroke 2.5px.
- Secondary latency (P50): #0078D4 (blue-strong), stroke 1.5px, dashed.
- Throughput area: gradient from #E6F0FF (bottom) to #B9DEFF (top).
- Tokens bars: #6C6CFF with 0.6 opacity.
- Cost ribbon: #FFB84D (amber) with 0.45 opacity.
- Failure/error overlays: #D9534F (red) with 0.12 opacity.
- Health badge rules: green (<=SLO), amber (SLO breached by <2x), red (>2x breach) — numeric thresholds tied to configured SLO.

Implementation notes / trade-offs discussed:
- Decided to use small-multiples rather than single multi-line for model variants to reduce line-overlap confusion in high-variance workloads.
- Chose EMA smoothing (3) to suppress noise while preserving peaks for incident detection.
- Backend must provide minute-level aggregates for latency percentiles and tokens; if minute aggregates unavailable, frontend should fall back to client-side downsampling and clearly annotate confidence.

Deliverables in this ticket:
- Figma prototype (compact card, expanded panel, small-multiples, rollout composer mock) + export-ready SVGs for icons.
- Detailed chart spec above and CSV schema.
- QA checklist for visual regression (color, stroke widths, legend correctness).

Next steps / acceptance criteria:
- Design review sign-off from product and eng (UX and infra).
- Developer implementation PR that matches tickbox spec: tooltip schema, export CSV, rollout overlay, and small-multiples behavior.
- Usability test with 5 engineers validating triage flow within 3 minutes.

Notes on metrics to track post-launch (for PM):
- Time to triage (average time from alert → open chart).
- Frequency of 'create rollout' from chart.
- Chart load success ratio and median render time.
